title: EEOC votes to propose new rule stripping feds of hearing rights, class action complaints
summary: Members of the public have just 30 days to digest and submit comments on a 130-page plan upending the process for alleging workplace discrimination at federal agencies.

title: NSA wants access to ‘all’ AI models, top official says
summary: The spy agency is taking a key role in the government’s new voluntary model-testing program, though its deputy director did not say which companies are participating.

title: Want to retire at the end of 2026? Start planning now
summary: OPM is still working through a sizable retirement backlog, and year-end retirees have plenty to sort out before they leave federal service.

title: Data from Labor employees seeking disability accommodations impacted by 'internal incident'
summary: The Labor Department is telling employees about an “internal incident report” in which an individual sent employees' sensitive health information to their personal email address.

title: Pushed out by the Trump administration, these ex-feds want to make agency firings simpler and fairer
summary: Across 12 cases that were analyzed for a new report on federal firing reform, it took an average 19 months for the underperforming employee to be removed or otherwise leave the position.

title: Lawmakers call for watchdog review of DOT’s passenger privacy practices
summary: The Transportation Department “has never taken a single enforcement action related to privacy,” Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore., and Rep. Shontel Brown, D-Ohio, said in a letter to the Government Accountability Office.

title: GSA's $13 billion fraud claim relies on cases predating task force
summary: The settlements cited add up to just $117 million, and at least one case predates the Trump administration.

title: Politicizing government investments hurts all of us
summary: COMMENTARY | What happens when political appointees, rather than career experts, get the final say over where federal dollars go?

title: Unions: OPM’s suitability and performance management overhauls assert ‘plenary’ authority over federal firing
summary: A coalition of labor groups sued the Trump administration Monday, arguing recent moves to centralize authority within the Office of Personnel Management and insert subjective criteria into employee evaluations amount to an end-run around the 1978 Civil Service Reform Act.

title: GSA says it’s uncovered ‘record-setting’ $13B in suspected procurement fraud
summary: The White House added General Services Administration fraud estimates to its website that serves as a ledger for suspected fraud across the federal government.

title: Agencies backfilled 20,600 employees who left government under the deferred resignation programs, analysis finds
summary: The Office of Personnel Management disputed the findings and countered that the analysis also shows around 85% of the DRP separations were not replaced.

title: State Department board’s ability to challenge firings undercut by DOJ
summary: Critics of the decision say the Justice Department's opinion is another step in the Trump administration's goal of making it easier to fire federal employees who are not fully aligned with its policy goals.

title: Blanche is confirmed. Now Congress needs to hold him accountable
summary: COMMENTARY | A former Justice Department staffer argues that Congress must protect whistleblowers and demand answers when the agency crosses the line.

title: White House space transportation policy calls for integration with air traffic control modernization
summary: The guidance directs the Transportation Department and other agencies to “implement a plan to integrate space launch and reentry management into airspace and traffic control modernization efforts.”

title: Unions accuse mediation agency of ‘doublespeak’ in updated lawsuit
summary: The Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service’s new policy allowing it to investigate the arbitrability of disputes if an agency objects to participating in them exceeds the “ministerial” agency’s authority, labor groups argue.

title: Postal inspectors aren’t being pulled away from mail crime investigations for immigration enforcement, IG reports
summary: The watchdog found that postal white collar crime investigations were not affected by “resource shifts.”

title: Watchdog: NSA’s NDAs don’t comply with whistleblower law
summary: As the Trump administration weighs instituting a standardized non-disclosure agreement for employees across government, one agency that already uses them routinely fails to educate workers about their whistleblower rights.

title: What AI’s workplace adoption means for government agencies
summary: COMMENTARY | Census data shows how workers are using AI in their everyday jobs, while government leaders are testing ways to bring those same practical uses into the public sector.

title: IRS CEO’s call to end advanced leave should be ‘null and void,’ NTEU says in lawsuit
summary: The National Treasury Employees Union argues Frank Bisignano running the IRS without Senate confirmation violates the Constitution.

title: ‘Glaring violations’ of the Hatch Act by senior Trump officials have gone unpunished for months, good government group alleges
summary: On Thursday, the Office of Special Counsel submitted disciplinary complaints against two federal employees over apparent Hatch Act violations.

title: House Democrats want answers on what CISA lost in workforce cuts
summary: Lawmakers want Congress’ watchdog to assess what capabilities were lost after the cyber agency shed roughly one-third of its staff.

title: Trump’s FDA pick faces questions about leading the agency
summary: Sen. Bill Cassidy, R-La., who will oversee her confirmation, says Dr. Heidi Overton’s management experience and role in the administration’s vaccine policy raise concerns.

title: Federal job listings provide clues for next set of Schedule P/C conversions
summary: New analysis from the Partnership for Public Service reveals that agencies have begun advertising positions as Schedule Policy/Career or planned for the at-will job category.

title: OPM wants to woo young workers. Can internet memes overcome Trump’s cuts to the civil service?
summary: An agency spokeswoman said that a four-person communications team — most younger than 30 — is spearheading the effort to make OPM’s social media more appealing to younger potential hires.

title: GSA looks to ‘meaningfully increase’ hiring to replenish its workforce
summary: Current and former GSA officials said significant hiring is needed at the Public Buildings Service to help the agency recover from last year’s deep staffing cuts.
